key_insight: OmniLiDAR introduces a single, text‑conditioned diffusion framework that models multiple LiDAR domains and sensing conditions jointly, enabling controllable synthesis across heterogeneous datasets without training separate models for each domain.
problem_solved: Current diffusion-based LiDAR generators are single-domain and require separate models for different sensors, environments, or conditions; OmniLiDAR addresses the need for unified, scalable generation that handles distribution shifts and enables controllable, multi-domain synthesis.
method: Train a unified diffusion model across multiple LiDAR datasets/modalities with explicit domain-aware conditioning (e.g., domain tokens or adapters) so a single model can represent diverse sensing distributions.

Use geometry-preserving input/output representations (range images / point-cloud-aware encoders and decoders) and a noise-aware denoising backbone to maintain realistic 3D structure during generation.
Provide controllable synthesis via text/attribute conditioning (sensor specs, weather, time, style) and a shared latent that supports domain transfer and fine-grained manipulation.
impact: OmniLiDAR enables scalable, cost‑effective generation of varied LiDAR scenes for simulation, data augmentation, and robust perception testing, reducing the need for expensive real-world data collection and multiple specialized models.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: unified diffusion pipeline with domain-conditioning tokens/adapters and geometry-preserving encoder/decoder.
Comparison grid: rows showing multiple target domains/conditions with side‑by‑side real vs. OmniLiDAR-generated point clouds or range images.
Control UI mockup: text/slider inputs (sensor range, density, weather) producing instant changes in generated LiDAR scenes.
Latent-space visualization + metrics: UMAP/t-SNE showing domain bridging and a small chart of fidelity/diversity tradeoffs across domains.
paper_title: OmniLiDAR: A Unified Diffusion Framework for Multi-Domain 3D LiDAR Generation
paper_authors: Youquan Liu, Weidong Yang, Ao Liang, Xiang Xu, Lingdong Kong
